about: The roof pattern's shared pieces (D290, tools/kits): one board (on edge along a verge and an eave, flat as flashing), one valley, and the frame and ridge every roof of the pattern lays unless its material has its own: a rafter, a batten under each course, and a ridge of two lapped boards for a covering with no ridge of its own. Each to its contract: its real size (dims: along, up, across, metres) and where its anchor is in it (anchor: from its low corner), the anchor seated by the layout on the roof's deck or its covering (roofing::on_covering), so one piece fits any covering. A material's own pieces override these by name.

valley.about: An open valley lined with two weathered boards, modelled; unfolded flat so it lies in the crease. Anchored at its middle on the deck.

verge.about: A weathered pine bargeboard, modelled. Anchored a centimetre under its top edge on its inner face: seated on the covering, it stands that much proud of it.

eave.about: A weathered pine fascia board, modelled. Anchored two centimetres over its top edge at its back: hung plumb from the deck's edge, under the covering.

flashing.about: A weathered board laid along a wall the roof meets, under the wall's drip, modelled. Anchored at its foot by the wall, on the covering.

rafter.about: A rafter or a ridge pole: a round pine pole in its bark.

batten.about: A sawn batten across the rafters, one under each course.

ridge.about: A ridge or hip cap for a covering with none of its own: two sawn boards lapped over the crest, the upper over the lower, laid flat so the game drapes them over a ridge's angle or a hip's, their ends eased round where the line stops.
